claim: Tens of thousands of civilians, including children, have been killed in Gaza.

heard.who: Gaza Health Ministry, as reported by the Associated Press (PBS), June 2025
heard.quote: The ministry says 55,104 people have been killed since the start of the war and 127,394 wounded.

heard.quote: says 7,797 children and 4,959 women were killed in Gaza as of April 30

answer: Many civilians, including thousands of children, have been killed in Gaza. No count here has been independently verified as separating fighters from civilians. The main total comes from the Gaza Health Ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, which mainly counts bodies reaching hospitals and does not separate civilians from fighters. The UN treats the total as reliable overall. In May 2024 the UN broke down only the fully identified dead: 7,797 children and 4,959 women by 30 April 2024. Two Lancet studies estimated the ministry undercounted. Israel says it killed more than 20,000 militants, without evidence. A parent can say: tens of thousands have been killed, no verified count separates civilians from fighters, and the ministry's total is disputed by some and treated as reliable by the UN.

The Associated Press found that in earlier wars the ministry's counts held up to UN and Israeli checks, and Reuters reports that Israel's military has accepted in briefings that the overall numbers are broadly reliable.

facts.text: Two peer-reviewed studies estimated that the ministry undercounted. A 2025 Lancet capture-recapture study estimated 64,260 deaths from traumatic injury to 30 June 2024 (95% interval 55,298 to 78,525), putting the ministry's count about 41 percent below the estimate (the estimate is about 70 percent above the ministry's 37,877). A 2026 Lancet Global Health household survey estimated 75,200 violent deaths to 5 January 2025, with the ministry's figure of 49,090 34.7 percent below that. Neither study estimates how many of the dead were fighters.

facts.text: In its six-month update report (covering 1 November 2023 to 30 April 2024) the UN human rights office said it had verified 8,119 killings in Gaza by 2 September 2024, including 2,036 women and 3,588 children. 'Verified' there means confirmed by at least three independent sources, so it counts only what the office could confirm; it is not a total and not a split between fighters and civilians. Of the 8,119, 7,607 were killed in residential buildings or similar housing, and of those 44 percent were children, 26 percent women and 30 percent men. The report adds that the large share killed in residential buildings is partly explained by its verification method.

facts.text: Researchers disagree on whether the ministry's figures are fabricated. Abraham Wyner, a Wharton statistician, argued in Tablet that the daily totals for 26 October to 10 November 2023 varied too little (about 270 a day, plus or minus about 15 percent) to be natural. Other researchers found no sign of inflation: UNRWA staff deaths compared with ministry totals made fabrication implausible, and a capture-recapture study found the ministry under-reported by 41 percent.

contested.text: The share of the dead who were civilians is the most disputed figure, and the ministry does not give it. The Associated Press analysed the ministry's data and called the share of women and children 'the best available proxy for civilian casualties'; it found that share fell from above 60 percent in October 2023 to below 40 percent in April 2024. A proxy is not a civilian count.

contested.text: The ministry is part of the Hamas-run government, which is why its figures are questioned. An Israeli army spokesman said in May 2024 that the military does not know how many civilians have been killed, and that Hamas does not either (NBC News). In October 2023 Israel said the ministry inflated the toll of a deadly explosion, after the ministry reported 500 dead and then lowered it to 471, while US intelligence agencies estimated 100 to 300 (AP).

not_claimed: This card does not say any single count is settled or exact.
It does not say all those killed were civilians, and it does not say most were fighters.
It does not deny that many civilians, including children, were killed.
It does not say how many of the dead were killed by Israeli forces and how many by other causes.
could_not_verify: I looked for an independent count of fighters among the dead and found none. The closest are the UN human rights office's verified subset (age and sex only) and a Guardian, +972 Magazine and Local Call report of a leaked Israeli database, which I could read only as a Guardian reprint and through CBC and Middle East Eye and which is not independently verified.

I could not find a reliable outlet or academic paper that examined Wyner's method in reply; the other scholarly checks (UNRWA staff comparison, capture-recapture, household survey) test the same question but are not direct replies to him. Jerusalem Post, JNS and Jewish Exponent pieces on Wyner repeat the Tablet article and are not counted as separate sources.
The Huynh, Chin and Spiegel Lancet letter of December 2023 (UNRWA staff deaths compared with the ministry's) could not be read; it is cited only through Khatib, McKee and Yusuf.
The method behind Israel's fighter counts (17,000-18,000 or 20,000) was not found in any source.

Fact 5 states what the UN human rights office's six-month update report says; the report is read in full and Al Jazeera and CBC (Reuters) confirm the 8,119 figure. News reports of this figure differ on the period (six months, seven months, eleven months) and some apply the 44 percent and 26 percent shares to all 8,119 deaths; the report itself applies them only to the 7,607 killed in residential buildings or similar housing.

Fact 6 (the leaked Israeli database of named fighters) is one Guardian, +972 Magazine and Local Call investigation. I read the Guardian's text through an Irish Examiner reprint (theguardian.com returned 404 and 972mag.com refused the fetch), and CBC and Middle East Eye only report it; none saw the data, and the Guardian says it has not viewed or verified the documents. I found no outlet that saw the documents or confirmed them with its own sourcing, so the fact counts as one source and stays short. To close it a person would need to read the investigation on theguardian.com or 972mag.com (21 August 2025) and find an independent outlet, such as Haaretz, that reached the same database.
LBC was removed as a source on this card: its page misstates the UN's view of the ministry's figures.

In May 2024 the UN broke down only the fully identified dead: 7,797 children and 4,959 women by 30 April 2024.

skeptic.notes: Round 3: checked the 8,119 fact against the OHCHR six-month update report itself (para 12): 'verified by OHCHR by 2 September 2024 standing at 8,119 ... including 2,036 women and 3,588 children'; of these 7,607 were killed in residential buildings, 44% children, 26% women, 30% men (of the 7,607, not of the 8,119); footnote 19: the residential share is partly explained by its method of at least three independent sources. Period: the report covers 1 Nov 2023 to 30 Apr 2024 but counts verified to 2 Sept 2024; the fact says so. All correct; I added the footnote 19 caveat. The misleading outlet is gone and the answer no longer uses the database. The answer sentences no longer rest on a short fact (facts 5 and 6 removed from answer_claims). Still short, so not verified: [must-fix] fact 5 has the record (OHCHR, read first-hand) and one reader (Al Jazeera); the record flag needs two readers and is_record on the OHCHR source. Add a second report of the same content, for example CBC/Reuters https://amp.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.7377967 (already on era5-hamas-and-civilian-areas), then set record true. [must-fix] fact 6 (Israeli database): one Guardian/+972/Local Call investigation seen through CBC and Middle East Eye, neither saw the data; fix only by the original investigation (theguardian.com or 972mag.com, August 2025) or a third outlet that saw the documents. Strongest objections: critics of Israel, no independent fighter/civilian split exists on the card; defenders, the ministry is Hamas-controlled. Both are stated.
